solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not much news as troops advance, not much

parts.note: a column is a body of troops marching in file
to inch is to advance by tiny amounts

explanation.surface: A war report: the soldiers creep forward only slightly, so there's little to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A column inch is a newspaper measure of space, one inch of a single column, so a tiny amount of copy.

clue.text: Food processed in Jersey perhaps with aspic in batter

parts.note: a Jersey cow chews and rechews its cud, food it has partly digested
aspic is a savoury jelly, a gel

explanation.surface: A cookery note: dish made in Jersey, with savoury jelly set in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks like the cook's mixture but is the verb to beat; Jersey is a breed of dairy cow as well as a Channel Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A club used for beating someone, and as a verb to beat with one, so batter is its synonym.

clue.text: Kind of paper changing political complexion in response to outside influence?

definitions.text: Kind of paper changing political complexion in response to outside influence?

parts.words: Kind of paper changing political complexion in response to outside influence?
parts.note: this test paper turns red or blue, the colours of the UK's main parties, when touched by acid or alkali

explanation.surface: A newspaper switches political allegiance under pressure from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain red is Labour and blue Conservative, the two colours this indicator paper shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists dip this dyed strip into a solution and it reddens with acids, blues with alkalis.

clue.text: Might such figures cause poets harm?

definitions.text: Might such figures cause poets harm?

parts.words: Might such figures cause poets harm?
parts.note: figures of speech that are jumbled up: the word for them, scrambled, spells out poets harm

explanation.surface: A worry that bad imagery could do writers damage.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: shuffle the letters of the second word and you get POETS HARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures of speech that combine incompatible images, a fault likely to embarrass a poet.

clue.text: Popular Socialist begins pressing rebel…

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the word Socialist begins with its first letter, which alone is used

parts.note: a pressing matter is an urgent one

explanation.surface: A well-liked leftist starts leaning on a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the next one in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a person who rises in revolt against authority, a rebel.

clue.text: …defender — tea party representative?

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
an MP, Member of Parliament, represents a party

explanation.surface: Following on from the rebel: a protector who stands for the Tea Party movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion, shortened informally, defends a title against challengers, so is its defender.

clue.text: Great online image?

parts.note: E is the prefix for electronic or online, as in e-mail
pic is short for picture, an image

explanation.surface: A query about whether a picture on the internet is a good one.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic is slang for tremendous or impressive, a casual synonym for great.

clue.text: Offensive contents of papers on Albania

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit inside the run of words papers on Albania, as its contents

explanation.surface: A diplomat finds the material in the dossier about Albania insulting.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal remarks are rude ones aimed at someone, so they are offensive.

clue.text: E.g. marine company receiving military medal as well as expression of admiration

indicators.note: the company takes the medal immediately after it, receiving it on its end

parts.note: MM is the Military Medal, a British decoration
and means as well as
O! is an exclamation of wonder

explanation.surface: A marine unit wins a decoration and admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: The Military Medal is a British award for bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: A Royal Marine is one example of a commando, a soldier trained for raids.

clue.text: Cultured chap, one upholding new version of Americanness

indicators.note: a new version of the letters reworks them into a different order

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: A cultivated man who stands up for a fresh form of being American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upholding' just places A above N in this down clue; together with AMERICANNESS those letters are rearranged by 'version of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with wide learning across many fields, an all-rounder with culture.

clue.text: Where to get clean and neat after relapsing, half-wasted

indicators.note: the cattle come after the turned letters
relapsing means going back, so the letters are read backwards
only half of the word wasted is kept, its latter half

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, an ox

explanation.surface: Advice for a drinker who has slipped back: get sober, having been half drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relapsing' turns TED, the back half of 'wasted', into DET.
explanation.definitionFit: A detox clinic is where addicts go to be cleansed of drink or drugs and become clean.

clue.text: Regularly using an old horse — but beating it won't make this move!

definitions.text: beating it won't make this move!

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of using an

parts.note: Red Rum is a famous racehorse, three-time winner of the Grand National in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A jockey on a veteran horse finds that whipping it won't make it go.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum was a British racehorse, winner of the Grand National steeplechase three times.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion instrument stays put however hard it is struck, unlike a horse being whipped.

clue.text: Country cure failing where trouble is internal

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
the trouble is placed inside the reworked letters
failing suggests the letters of cure have gone wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A nation where medicine fails because the problem lies inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is the definition; 'cure' looks like part of the story but is the fodder 'failing' works on.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic on the Pacific coast of South America, straddling the equator.

clue.text: Portugal and Italy getting a loan arrangement from which notes are automatically forthcoming

definitions.text: from which notes are automatically forthcoming

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters puts them in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Two countries arrange a loan from which banknotes flow automatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' looks like money, given the loan, but means musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A player piano, worked by perforated rolls, that plays music without a pianist.

clue.text: Having drifted, lies stranded here?

indicators.note: having drifted suggests the letters have moved out of place and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A castaway, having floated away, lies marooned on some shore.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An uninhabited isle where a castaway would wash up and be marooned after floating at sea.

clue.text: Bird changes colour

parts.note: turns means changes, as milk turns
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A bird that alters its hue, like a chameleon.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wading shorebird that flips over pebbles looking for food.

clue.text: Greenish-blue clothing for you and I, a bit of linen

indicators.note: clothing means covering, so the outer word wraps round the others

parts.note: teal is a greenish-blue colour
to can mean for, as in a toast to someone
you and I together are we

explanation.surface: A greenish-blue garment for the two of us, made from a scrap of linen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth for drying dishes, kept with the household linen.

clue.text: Finally reversing direction towards end avoids unknown part of frozen ocean

indicators.note: the compass point near the end flips, south becoming north

parts.note: at last means finally

indicators.note: avoids means the unknown is left out

parts.note: icy means frozen
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A ship near journey's end turns round to escape an uncharted bit of polar sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of frozen ocean' tempts toward the Arctic; 'ocean' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The second largest of the world's seas, between Europe and the Americas.

clue.text: Old farm machinery enthusiast found way of dealing with unpleasant smells

definitions.text: way of dealing with unpleasant smells

parts.note: ex means former or old
a tractor is farm machinery
a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: A vintage tractor buff discovers how to cope with bad smells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen or bathroom device that sucks out stale air and odours.

clue.text: Sailor drunk and embarrassed

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
a lush is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A sailor, tipsy and red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Blushing, red in the face from shame, as an embarrassed person is.

clue.text: Don't retire on lousy payouts when nothing's left

indicators.note: lousy means poor or bad, so the letters are reworked
left means gone, so the zero is removed

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A worker told not to give up the job on a meagre pension once the money runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' looks like leaving work but means going to bed; 'left' drops O from PAYOUTS before 'lousy' rearranges PAYUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay up is to not go to bed, and retire can mean to go to bed.

clue.text: Container docked by trains

indicators.note: docked means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a tea chest is a wooden packing box

explanation.surface: A shipping container unloaded in the dock from the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' and 'trains' suggest a port and railway, but 'docked' cuts the tail and 'trains' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach is to instruct or coach, so trains is its synonym in the third person.

clue.text: In speech, Irishman is clipped, not woolly

indicators.note: in speech means as said aloud, so the sound of the name counts

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name

explanation.surface: An Irishman's speech is crisp and precise, not vague.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the name and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep that has been sheared is clipped and no longer covered in wool.

clue.text: Draw off last of old wine barrel with antique instrument

parts.note: sack is an old name for sherry-like white wine

indicators.note: the final letter of the barrel word is drawn off

parts.note: a butt is a large cask

explanation.surface: Tapping the dregs of an aged wine cask, alongside a vintage instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw off' sounds like drawing wine, but it removes the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An early trombone of the Renaissance, a historical brass instrument.

clue.text: Washington's international force not in Oman at first for aquatic exercise?

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

indicators.note: not means the following word is left out

parts.note: Interpol is the international police organisation

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of Oman

explanation.surface: An American international police team is absent from a Gulf state's first operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A team sport played by swimmers in a pool, so exercise done in the water.

clue.text: Shy youth leader follows sumo wrestling

indicators.note: the youth's leader comes after the reworked letters
wrestling means twisting, so the letters of sumo are rearranged
the leader of youth is its first letter

explanation.surface: A timid young chief trails behind the sumo wrestlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouse-like in manner, quiet and timid, so shy.

clue.text: Vermin's headcount 95 per cent reduced, but still vermin

indicators.note: the head letter is a Roman numeral, a count of a thousand; cut by 95 per cent it becomes fifty

parts.note: mice are vermin

explanation.surface: Pest control cuts a rodent population drastically, yet pests remain.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the Roman 1000; 95 per cent off leaves 50, Roman L, so the head of MICE changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Parasitic insects living on hair, regarded as vermin.

clue.text: Work experience in prison hulk?

parts.note: to intern is to imprison, hold in prison
a hulk is an old ship, once used as a floating prison

explanation.surface: Is serving time on a prison hulk a kind of job placement?
explanation.walkthrough: Prison hulks were old ships used to hold British convicts.
explanation.definitionFit: A placement in which a trainee gains practical work experience.
